fields.Front: Why are rocks the most stable and oldest records of past events?
fields.Back: Because the chemical bonds in the most common rock type, the SILICATES, are extremely hard to break. To know the age of a rock containing evidence of an event is to date that event.

fields.Front: Compare the ages other cultures gave for Earth's origin with Ussher's.
fields.Back: Ussher (1650): 4004 B.C., barely over 6000 years. Maya calendar: more than 400 million years. Hindu calendar: the present world came into existence almost 2 billion years ago.

fields.Front: Why is Earth's age taken as 4.54 billion years, from meteorites?
fields.Back: Meteorites as a whole (fragments broken from asteroids) average 4.54 Ga, and Earth gradually accreted from the same solids that compose the asteroids. Building Earth may have taken a few million years or as much as 100 million years, but at 4.54 Ga the building was well underway. 'If you are ever asked the age of Earth, reply: 4.54 billion years.'

fields.Front: Why can't we pick up a chunk of the very oldest rock made on Earth?
fields.Back: Plate tectonics (Chapter 3) constantly recycles old material. That is why we look to meteorites/asteroids for Earth's age, and why the oldest surviving material is a mineral (zircon) incorporated inside a younger rock.

fields.Front: Name the two oldest crustal fragments on Earth, where they are, and their ages.
fields.Back: Both in Canada: Acasta Gneiss, Northwest Territories, 4.031 +/- 0.003 Ga; Nuvvuagittuq Greenstone, Quebec, 4.388 Ga or 3.75 Ga (disputed). Neither is as old as the original crust.

fields.Front: What is the oldest matter known, and what does its age date?
fields.Back: Meteorites obtained from primitive asteroids, representing material formed as the Solar System first took shape; consistently 4.567 billion years - a rough age for the Solar System.

fields.Front: Why can sediments usually not be dated absolutely?
fields.Back: Their grains are recycled from older rocks, so an isotopic age would date the source rock, not the time of deposition. Relative age dating is used instead (slides).

fields.Text: Age of the Solar System = {{c1::4.567}} Ga (oldest matter: meteorites from primitive asteroids). Age of Earth = {{c1::4.54}} Ga. Oldest mineral, a {{c1::zircon}} crystal = {{c1::4.404}} Ga.
About {{c1::4.48}} billion years ago a planet the size of present-day {{c1::Mars}}, called {{c1::Theia}}, impacted Earth and completely {{c1::melted}} both bodies.
Notation: {{c1::Ga}} = billion years, {{c1::Ma}} = million years, {{c1::ka}} = thousand years, {{c1::a}} = year; so 4.567 Ga = {{c1::4,567}} Ma = 4,567,000,000 a.
